title: Runway shift — concise log (late-night handoff)
content:
Quick summary (for next person)
- Quiet-ish night overall but a couple of noisy spikes in tail latency for hosted text-gen (us-west) between 22:05–23:00 PST.
- Resolved primary incident (INF-4823) by enabling burst capacity + reverting to fp16 variant for rw-v2 in the affected pool.
- One follow-up outstanding: embedder queue buildup for high-concurrency customer (ticket INF-4999). Needs coordination with SE tomorrow.

What happened (timeline)
- 21:58: Alerts start: latency_p95_textgen_us_west > 1200ms, p99 drifting. Routing dashboard shows requests backing up into the m40-pool-2 queue.
- 22:03: Confirmed heavy batching + long sequences from a single customer job (customer C-102). This pushed KV cache memory high and triggered autoscaler stall (scale cooldown prevented immediate scale-up).
- 22:08: Took emergency action: toggled burst capacity for customer-tier A on the control plane and switched model variant back to fp16 for the pool. Latency fell back to baseline by ~22:25.
- 22:30: Follow-up: rolled planned restart of inference-workers in that pool to clear stuck KV entries; graceful rolling restart, no erroring requests observed after.

Commands I ran (notes)
- Check queue sizes: curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://control-plane.redwood.ai/v1/pools/m40-pool-2/metrics | jq '.queues'
- Increase burst cap (UI is fine but CLI used): curl -X POST https://control-plane.redwood.ai/v1/pools/m40-pool-2/burst -d '{"delta":4}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
- Switch model variant (temporary): curl -X POST https://control-plane.redwood.ai/v1/routes/default/switch -d '{"model":"rw-v2-fp16"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
- Rolling restart (k8s bastion): ssh gpu-bastion && kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-worker -n us-west --context=us-west-prod
- Clear small prefix cache (only if safe): redis-cli -h cache-usw1 KEYS 'kvcache:rw-v2:*' | xargs -r redis-cli -h cache-usw1 DEL

Why I switched the model variant
- The q8 candidate (rw-v2-q8) was cheaper but started producing intermittent OOMs under heavy KV pressure in m40-pool-2; memory fragmentation + long sequences made the quantized path unstable in that pool. Reverting to fp16 fixed the immediate availability problem. We'll still want to test q8 under a constrained staging profile and maybe tune allocator flags. See PR #812 for allocator tweaks I opened (linked above).

Open items / follow-ups (owners included)
- INF-4999 (Priya): investigate embedder queue skew for customer C-102; add request throttling or per-customer batching limits. Customer facing note required.
- Autoscaler cooldown tweak (Liam): extend aggressive policy for burst-enabled pools; current cooldown 60s too long for sudden spikes.
- Long-term: run q8 stressmatrix (me + ML infra) with long-token bursts to reproduce OOM patterns and evaluate allocator flags (PR #812).
- Add a canary route that uses q8 only for low-concurrency routes (product + runtime). Ticket created, link in Jira.

Things to watch on next shift (top-of-pager)
- Textgen p99 / p95 in us-west and eu-west: if p99 > 1.2s for > 5m escalate.
- embedder-queue-depth (redis) > 5000 for > 2m: likely customer hotspot.
- GPU memory fragmentation alerts on m40-pool-* (OOM patterns).

Quick playbook (short)
1) If p99 textgen spikes: look at routing dashboard to see whether requests are concentrated on a single customer or route.
2) If single-customer: manually enable burst for that customer on the control plane and consider switching variant to fp16 in that pool.
3) If OOMs observed: scale down q8 consumers, revert variant, open memory dump ticket (artifact: /var/log/inference/memdump).
4) If queues keep growing despite burst: escalate to on-call SRE lead and open a short-lived rate-limit for that tenant.

Escalation contacts
- Primary on-call SRE lead: Liam Chen (Slack: @liam) — ping #sre-pager, then DM.
- SE owner for C-102: Priya Desai (Slack: @priya) — include customer notes if throttling is applied.
- Pager fallback: PagerDuty schedule -> +1-555-0100 (use PD).

Notes to next shift (practical)
- I left the burst capacity +4 in m40-pool-2. If traffic quiets, please remove it (control-plane/API or UI) to avoid cost drift.
- Rolling restart completed at 22:32; check pods with kubectl get pods -n us-west | grep inference-worker and verify Ready==1.
- I did a quick health check on the model-quality monitor for fp16; no deviation in generation quality observed in spot checks but we should run the nightly eval tomorrow.

Temporary procedures I scribbled while troubleshooting (for doc cleanup later)
- validate-allocator.sh: small script to run memprof on a sample load (staging only). Location: ~/scripts/validate-allocator.sh (needs cleanup & PR).
- quick-fallback.sh: curl to switch route model variant and a follow-up check on /metrics to ensure tokens/sec climbs back. TODO: wrap in a safe-lock to avoid repeated oscillation.

Questions / things I couldn't finish
- Reproduce exact sequence that caused fragmentation — didn't have a long enough load window; need a synthetic generator that mimics C-102 pattern (long tokens + burst).
- Decide if q8 should be restricted by route or pool by default. Product input required.

Next-shift checklist (5 min)
- Check control plane burst settings (m40-pool-2).
- Verify textgen p95/p99 for us-west and eu-west.
- Touch base with Priya if embedder queue > 1000.
- Run quick smoke: curl health endpoint for three routes: /v1/generate (default), /v1/embed, /v1/chat and confirm 200 + latency under SLAs.

If anything urgent ping me (Slack @aisha) or escalate via PD. Signed off — Aisha
